question.worked_solution:
Remember that the square root of a perfect square can be simplified using absolute value.

$$
\sqrt{{x}^{2}}=|x|
$$

Also, we notice that ${p}^{2},81,$ and ${q}^{2}$ are all perfect squares.

First, we write the expression under the square root as a perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{\frac{{p}^{2}}{81{q}^{2}}} & =\sqrt{\frac{{p}^{2}}{{9}^{2}\cdot {q}^{2}}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{p\cdot p}{9\cdot 9\cdot q\cdot q}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{p\cdot p}{9\cdot q\cdot 9\cdot q}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{p}{9q}\cdot \frac{p}{9q}} \\  & =\sqrt{{(\frac{p}{9q})}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we take the absolute value of the squared quantity and simplify using the rules of absolute value:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{{(\frac{p}{9q})}^{2}} & =|\frac{p}{9q}| \\  & =\frac{|p|}{|9q|} \\  & =\frac{|p|}{|9|\cdot |q|} \\  & =\frac{|p|}{9|q|}\end{aligned}
$$
